release: Windows Defender Picker Compatibility & Release Gate Hardening
name: Windows Defender Picker Compatibility & Release Gate Hardening
changes: Rebuilds NewzDeckPicker.exe with normal Go build metadata instead of the stripped -s -w -buildid= profile after Microsoft Defender flagged the v3.6.89 Portable ZIP as Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml specifically through NewzDeckPicker.exe.
Keeps NewzDeckPicker.go source behavior unchanged while using the same -H windowsgui metadata-retaining strategy that previously resolved the NewzDeckYenc.exe Defender false-positive condition.
Adds explicit Picker build provenance to SOURCE_MANIFEST.json and release-time checks requiring a normal Go build ID and symbol table for NewzDeckPicker.exe.

Forces the canonical Windows release checkout back to LF/no-autocrlf before hash-based regression guards run so reviewed payload hashes are evaluated against canonical Git bytes rather than CRLF-converted working-tree files.
Makes native Python, Node and Go validation failures fatal in the GitHub Actions release gate instead of allowing a PowerShell step to continue after a nonzero native-command exit code.
Preserves all v3.6.89 Automation, Wanted, Smart Import, Newsgroup Browser and SABnzbd 5.1.2 behavior; this release changes Windows build/release hardening plus version identity only.
regression_guards: NewzDeckPicker.go remains byte-for-byte the published v3.6.89 source while build-portable.py gives only Picker the normal-metadata -H windowsgui build profile.
Portable payload validation requires NewzDeckPicker.exe to expose a non-empty Go build ID and symbol table and records its build override in SOURCE_MANIFEST.json.
The release workflow enforces canonical LF checkout before payload-hash guards and enables PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference so any guard failure stops publication.
All v3.6.82-v3.6.89 application regression guards are carried forward with v3.6.90 payload fingerprints.
Defender-clean NewzDeckYenc.exe provenance and frozen application/browser behavior remain unchanged.
